claims.text: Friction stir welding repair will mitigate hot cracking relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
Friction stir welding repair will preserve the component's mechanical integrity under aggressive operating conditions.
The target material is susceptible to hot cracking during thermal fusion processes.
Friction stir welding is a non-fusion, solid-state repair process.
Friction stir welding mechanically stirs and refines the microstructure without reaching the melting temperature.
Suitable tool rotation and traverse speed can maintain sub-melting-temperature repair conditions.
The repair will produce a refined, fine-grained microstructure in the repaired zone.
The repaired zone will have reduced residual stresses.
The repaired zone will be free of fusion-induced defects.
Friction stirring induces severe plastic deformation and dynamic recrystallization.
Severe plastic deformation and dynamic recrystallization refine the grains in the repaired zone.
Grain refinement and elimination of crack-promoting regions suppress hot cracking.
The proposed mechanism will restore and may enhance mechanical properties compared with fusion-welded repairs.
Friction-stir-repaired components will have higher fracture toughness than fusion-welded controls.
Friction-stir-repaired components will have longer fatigue life than fusion-welded controls.
Friction-stir-repaired components will exhibit significantly less hot cracking than fusion-welded controls.
Traditional fusion-welding repair produces hot cracking and compromised performance under aggressive service conditions.
